engagement_title: Anvil and Oak Strength movement library: cut six demo takes into one library, bring the poster frames to a single studio white, recover the wordmark and the certification seal off a photographed patch, and rebuild the printer's exercise card into a live six record run
vertical: Health, Wellness and Fitness. Subscription strength training app with a coached movement library, sold direct at 49 dollars a month to home gym subscribers, filmed in a converted barn gym outside Burlington, Vermont
real_brief_anchor: Adapted from the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, where a personal training business with a large exercise library wanted a repeatable production pipeline turning raw demo footage into short educational reference clips with reusable branding, muscle group callouts, and a clip naming and organisation convention. Two parts of that literal ask are on the connector's unavailable list and are therefore re carved rather than faked: open timeline editing to timestamps and frame by frame overlay or caption compositing do not exist here, so the callouts become a printed and authored reference card set that lives beside each clip rather than burned into it, which is what a coached library actually ships to subscribers anyway. Everything else in the post is real work and fully doable: shortening long demo takes into per movement highlights, producing the vertical companions the app's short feed needs, bringing a set of poster frames shot across two sessions to one studio white, recovering the studio's own mark and certification seal from the only surviving physical object, and turning the printer's existing exercise card into a live six record run so the library extends itself later. The business is laundered to a fully invented studio, Anvil and Oak Strength, run by fictional coaches Ruth Callaway and Dean Marchetti. No real trainer, gym, certifying body or app is referenced, and the certification seal is a coined in house mark rather than any real credential.
client_one_liner: Six movements are filmed, the takes are far too long, the poster frames were shot on two different days and do not match, and our logo only exists on a stitched patch we can photograph.
client_brief:
Anvil and Oak Strength, movement library build

We are two coaches with a subscription app. Subscribers pay monthly and the thing they use most is the movement library, which is a short reference clip per exercise with a card beside it. We are rebuilding the first six core movements and then we will add six more every quarter, so whatever you set up has to be something we can run again.

Here is what we have. Each movement was filmed as one long demo take, sometimes two or three takes, and they are far too long to put in front of anybody. There is a lot of setting up the bar at the front, and there is a rep in some of them that did not go well. We need a short landscape clip per movement that shows the movement being done properly, and a tall version of each for the short feed.

Our photographer came in and shot stills while we filmed. Those are the poster frames for each movement and they have to look like one studio. They do not right now. She was in twice and the light was not the same both times, and I think a bulb had been changed.

Dean recorded the coaching cues for each movement in one sitting. It is usable but the barn is a barn.

The cards. We had six exercise cards printed last year and the printer still has our file, which we have. We need six new cards, one per movement, each with its own poster frame, its own name, its own cue list and its own muscle group line. The cue lists are not all the same length.

Our mark and our certification seal only exist stitched onto a patch on our gym bags. We need both back as artwork, because they go on every card and on the library sheet.

And we need a library reference sheet we can update ourselves as movements get added.

We charge forty nine a month. It should look like a real coach's studio, not a gym chain and not a physiotherapy clinic.
price_band_and_audience: Coached strength subscription at 49 dollars a month, subscriber 30 to 52, home gym or garage gym, already lifting and buying instruction rather than motivation. The band is load bearing in both directions. Drop toward a 9 dollar mass fitness app and the correct treatment is high saturation, hard contrast, big shouty type, bodies as motivation imagery, cards that are mostly a photograph; ship that here and the coaching claim collapses, because the subscriber is paying for someone who knows what a hip hinge is and that person does not shout. Push up toward a clinical or rehabilitation register and it becomes cold, white, diagrammatic and medical, which reads as physiotherapy, is a different product, and is exactly the thing this studio's whole positioning is not. The correct register is a working craftsman's studio: one honest studio white, real bodies doing real work, quiet confident type, cue lists that read as instruction rather than as marketing. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed with a per quarter extension attached.

brand_identity.sector: Subscription strength training app with a coached movement library, sold direct to home gym subscribers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, outside Burlington, Vermont, a two coach studio filmed in a converted barn gym.
brand_identity.about: Anvil and Oak Strength is a coached strength subscription run by two coaches, Ruth Callaway and Dean Marchetti, out of a converted barn gym outside Burlington. Subscribers pay monthly for a movement library: a short reference clip per exercise with a card beside it, rebuilt six movements at a time and extended every quarter. The promise is competence rather than motivation, someone who knows what a hip hinge is, teaching it plainly.
brand_identity.audience: Subscribers aged 30 to 52 with a home or garage gym, already lifting and paying for instruction rather than motivation. They can tell a coach from a cheerleader and buy the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: 49 dollars a month, coached strength, extended a quarter at a time. Positioned as a working coach's studio: clearly above a 9 dollar mass fitness app and deliberately clear of a clinical or rehabilitation register.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a sturdy, slightly condensed slab or grotesque with real weight and confidence. Text: a plain, legible humanist sans. The cue list is the hardest role, instruction read while someone is under a bar, so it favours clarity over character. No gym chain italics and no clinical thin weights.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, instructional and calm. Speaks like a coach giving a cue, not a brand selling one. Example line: 'Brace, hinge, drive through the floor. That is the whole lift.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark and the in house certification seal survive only as stitching on a canvas gym bag patch, held now as one handheld photograph. Both have to be recovered from that photograph as artwork before they can go on the cards and the library sheet. The seal is a compound ring lockup, type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring. There is no vector file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Competence and honesty: real bodies doing real work, taught by people who actually lift.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_demo_takes/ (14 files across 6 movements)
assets_supplied.kind: Long single camera demo takes, two or three per movement, filmed in one session in the barn gym.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every movement, all the takes. They are far too long and there is a lot of setting up at the front."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The takes carry their most visible motion in the setup and in the reset after a failed rep rather than in the working set, so a shortening pass driven by what is happening on screen returns a plausible, well paced clip of the wrong part of the take at exactly the requested length. Separately two of the fourteen were filmed against the mirrored end wall, so the plate reads reversed and the coach appears to be loading the bar with the wrong hand, and one movement's only usable take is a 1080p phone recording rather than the camera master.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_poster_stills/ (6 frames plus alternates)
assets_supplied.kind: Studio stills shot by a photographer alongside the filming, across two separate visits a fortnight apart.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The poster frames. She was in twice and the light was not the same both times."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A ceiling bank was replaced between the two visits, so the second session's frames carry a different illuminant that one identical correction applied across the set cannot resolve, and the difference is small enough per frame to look acceptable alone. In two frames the chrome of the loaded bar sits at almost the luminance of the barn's whitewashed wall, so a subject led cut bites the bar sleeve while returning a clean looking edge everywhere else.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_cues.wav
assets_supplied.kind: Dean's spoken coaching cues for all six movements, recorded in one sitting in the gym.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The cues, one sitting, all six. It is usable but the barn is a barn."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The room's reverb sits on the sibilants rather than as broadband noise, so cleanup lifts intelligibility while leaving the tail of each cue ringing, and the ringing is audible only when a cue is heard immediately before the next one rather than in isolation.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_exercise_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer used for last year's exercise card set: a portrait card with a picture box, a movement name, a muscle group line, and a fixed cue list block down the lower two thirds.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The file the printer worked from. Same card, six new movements."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The cue list block is a fixed frame that does not spill. Records whose cue list runs longer than last year's simply stop rendering at the frame's edge, mid line and without a mark, while the merge reports success and the page count still matches the record count.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_patch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a stitched cloth patch on a canvas gym bag, carrying the studio wordmark in one thread colour and, beside it, a circular certification seal with type set around a central anvil glyph inside a ruled ring.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark and the seal. This patch is the only place either of them still exists."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The seal is a compound ring lockup, and a single prompt for it returns the type ring while silently dropping the inner rule and the central glyph at an entirely plausible looking result, while background removal on the ring hands back a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The thread also raises a visible nap on the wordmark's strokes, which reads as texture at full frame and as broken edges once traced.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_library.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The six movements with their names, muscle group lines, cue lists as approved by both coaches, and the clip naming convention the app expects.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six movements and their cues. The naming convention is what our app reads."

acceptance_bar: Each of the six landscape highlights shows the movement actually being performed correctly from setup through the working set, not the bar being loaded and not a failed rep. A clip of the right length showing the wrong part of the take is not delivered.
No clip is delivered reversed. A movement in which the coach appears to work the wrong side fails outright, because subscribers copy what they see.
No delivered file, raster or video, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, and no crop, resize or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

The six poster frames read as one studio when laid side by side: one white point, one black point, one warmth, with the whitewashed wall reading as the same wall in all six. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
Where a poster frame carries a cut subject, the cut holds along the loaded bar as well as along the body.
The card set is one press ready file of six pages, one movement per page in the library order, each carrying its own poster frame, name, muscle group line and complete cue list.
Every cue list is complete on the page. A card whose cue list stops mid line at the edge of its block fails even though the page count is right.

The wordmark and the seal are placeable artwork rather than pictures of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and both still readable at the size they actually reproduce on the card and on the library sheet against its deep ground, with the seal's inner rule and central glyph present and its counters open.

The library sheet arrives as one working file the coaches can extend themselves, canvases keeping their own sizes, with the words as text they can retype and the marks as live vector shapes, delivered alongside the self contained source it was built from.
The cleaned cue audio reads as one coach speaking in a good room, heard as a continuous run of cues and not only cue by cue.
One type system across the cards and the library sheet, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
Every delivered clip and frame is named to the convention the app reads, and the note states per movement which take was used and why.

adobe_surfaces.role: Turns fourteen long demo takes into six usable highlights and their vertical companions, and makes a barn recording listenable. The summariser is how the agent reads takes it did not film, the shortening cutter is the only instrument available and it chooses its own moments inside whatever it is handed, the resizer produces the vertical without ever adding a pixel, and speech cleanup has to be judged across a run of cues rather than on one.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Brings six poster frames shot under two different ceiling banks to one studio white, cuts the card picture boxes without enlarging anything, and recovers both a wordmark and a compound ring seal at thread level off a photographed cloth patch, with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (including its validator mode), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the printer's flat card artwork into a live six record merge with a per row poster frame binding, then renders the press file and the per record proofs. This is the surface that makes the quarterly extension real: the next six movements are rows, not a new commission.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express, asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The library reference sheet as one native editable document at more than one canvas size, which is what lets the coaches add movements themselves. Every frame must be embedded as image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, both marks go in as inline vector so they stay editable, and family and weight are declared on every text element or the type falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed type system carrying the cards and the library sheet, where the cue lists are the hardest typographic problem in the job because they are instruction that has to be read while someone is under a bar. The recommender refuses to pair, weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, and one bad name kills the entire kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the studio does not have, a plate rack and chalk texture band for the library sheet header, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative candidates excluded and graded into the same studio white as the six. The Boards half persists the shortlist the two coaches sign off from, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface, given that the library has to extend itself every quarter.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are a genuine one record per page run and belong on the merge surface precisely because the next six movements are rows; the library sheet has to be a free form canvas the coaches edit. The brief pins both, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role and against the app's naming convention.
trajectory.judgement: The naming convention is a deliverable requirement, not housekeeping, so it is applied at ingest rather than retrofitted at the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by movement and role.

trajectory.action: Summarise all fourteen takes to read what is actually in each one, since the agent did not film them and cannot scrub them.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen long takes made by somebody else are opaque, and the client's own account of them (setup at the front, a bad rep in some) is a rough memory rather than a map. Which take per movement is the working one is the first real decision in the job.
trajectory.produces: A per take content map and a first choice of source take per movement.

trajectory.action: Cut each movement's landscape highlight from its chosen take with the shortening cutter, then watch each returned clip.
trajectory.judgement: The cutter only shortens and it selects its own moments inside what it is handed, so the only lever is which take it is handed and how long the result is asked to be. The response reports a duration, not a subject.
trajectory.produces: Six landscape highlights with the source take recorded for each.

trajectory.action: Produce the vertical companion for each movement from the landscape highlight, reading the returned dimensions against the source.
trajectory.judgement: The resizer never adds pixels, so a source that is not a camera master cannot reach the short feed's spec and that has to be found here rather than at delivery.
trajectory.produces: Six vertical companions with their returned dimensions recorded, and a note of any movement that could not reach spec.

trajectory.action: Clean the coaching cue recording, then listen to it as a continuous run of cues rather than cue by cue.
trajectory.judgement: A barn's reverb is not broadband noise and cleanup treats it as though it were. Each cue heard alone sounds fine; the question is what happens where one cue ends and the next begins.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned cue track with a written note on what the cleanup resolved and what it did not.

trajectory.action: Preview the six poster frames and their alternates, triaging which visit each belongs to by its own light rather than by its filename, and reading true dimensions against the card's picture box.
trajectory.judgement: The client says the light was not the same both times and thinks a bulb was changed. The frames are the only thing that can settle which is which, and the difference is small enough per frame to be invisible unless they are compared.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering illuminant, tilt, subject contrast against the wall, and true dimensions against every destination.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a barn floor is rarely the horizon the camera thought it was.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one studio white from the frame that best represents the room and bring each of the six toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, and a set shot under two different ceiling banks cannot be reached by one identical parameter set. The whitewashed wall is the reference surface because it is the thing that appears in all six.
trajectory.produces: Six graded poster frames at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the poster frames where the card design needs the subject clear of its ground, selecting by the material's own visual properties, and inspect each cut edge along the bar as well as along the body.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate and a subject led cut has no contrast to work with where chrome meets whitewash. A clean edge on the body is not evidence about the bar.
trajectory.produces: Cut poster frames with their edges inspected, and a record of which needed a different route.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark and the seal off the patch: thread level selections naming each mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, bounds crops driven by the selections' own returned boxes, traces, then viewBoxes injected and the opaque full canvas ground paths removed.
trajectory.judgement: Four decisions no tool makes: how to word each selection so it takes thread and not canvas, whether the compound ring can be taken in one selection or has to be built from its parts, which polarity to trace, and whether the nap the stitching raises is texture worth keeping or noise to be resolved before tracing.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark and seal, plus colour accurate variants.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the plate rack and chalk texture band, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution, and grade it into the studio white.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the studio target rather than the strongest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 49 dollar coached band: a working studio rather than a gym chain or a clinic. The cue list is the hardest role because it is read under load, and the weight cannot be inferred from a style name.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's press PDF to a working document, export its interchange form, and read the real frame inventory and the true bounds of the cue list block.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anybody's control, and the bounds of the block that has to carry six different cue lists are a fact about the document rather than a design choice.
trajectory.produces: A converted template plus a written inventory of its real text and picture frames with their bounds.

trajectory.action: Generate the mapping readout, compose the field mapping for name, muscle group line, cue list and the per row poster frame against the document's own story text, validate it, and prepare the merge template.
trajectory.judgement: Offsets are computed against the document's true story rather than against a convenient summary of it, and the validator's verdict is a statement about shape, not about whether the fields land.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template verified to carry every expected field.

trajectory.action: Merge the six records with the per row poster frame binding, render the press file and the per record proofs, and read every page.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to record count is necessary and not sufficient, and multi record raster output returns in an order whose labels misreport it, so identity and completeness are confirmed on the page.
trajectory.produces: A six page press file, per record proofs, and a page by page identity and completeness check.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the library sheet at its canvas sizes, embed every frame as image data, place the wordmark and the seal as inline vector inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers at the size they will actually reproduce on the deep ground, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a reference is not a frame, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how the six movements read as one library rather than six posters.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit of the others.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded frames and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note and the naming manifest.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success response is partial success, and vector is not boardable so the marks belong in the note. The note has to be specific enough that the next quarter's six movements are a repeat rather than a rediscovery.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, plus the written handover and the naming manifest.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each highlight actually shows the movement being performed. The shortening pass selects its own moments from inside the take according to what is happening on screen, and in these takes the most visible activity is the bar being loaded at the front and the reset after a rep that did not go well, not the smooth working set. What comes back is a well paced clip of exactly the requested length with a plausible beginning and end, and the response reports only a duration. Which of the fourteen takes this happens to is a property of where each take's activity sits, which is not visible in the take's length, its filename or its summary, and can be established only by cutting it and watching the result.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the tool exposes no way to say which part of the take matters, so a competent agent cannot get it right first time except by luck, and the take it chose was chosen from a summary of content rather than of pacing. (b) Nothing states it: the client says only that there is a lot of setting up at the front and a bad rep in some of them, which is a description of the raw material, not of what a cutter will select from it. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different source, not the same call again: hand the cutter a different take of the same movement whose activity sits on the working set, or ask for a different target length so the selection window falls elsewhere, and re judge each result by watching it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re read the content maps for where activity sits rather than for what is present, re cut the affected movements from different takes or at a different target length, and watch every returned clip through before any of them is named to the convention.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A movement library in which subscribers are shown a coach loading a bar or resetting after a failed rep as the reference for how the exercise is performed, on a product whose entire claim is coaching competence.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every cue list is actually on its card. The cue block inherited from the printer's artwork is a fixed frame, and a fixed frame does not spill: a record whose cue list runs longer than the one the frame was drawn for simply stops rendering at the frame edge, mid line and without any mark that anything is missing. The merge reports success, the page count still equals the record count, and each page looks like a properly composed card. Which of the six overflow depends on the frame's true bounds against the applied type size and the actual cue text, and none of those three are knowable together until the pages exist.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right first time would require knowing the rendered depth of six different cue lists inside a frame whose bounds came from somebody else's document, which nothing reports; and no ordering helps, because the overflow only exists once the type system and the real copy meet the inherited frame. (b) Nothing states it. The client says only that the cue lists are not all the same length, which is a fact about the copy, not a disclosure that a frame silently truncates. The acceptance line about complete cue lists is the client's own requirement, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a design decision with consequences: change the type role's size or leading for the whole set so the longest record fits, which changes every card, or re cut the copy with the coaches, or re map the cue list into a different frame if the document has one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Measure the longest record against the block by rendering it, re decide the cue role's size and leading for the entire set rather than for one card, re prepare and re merge, then read every page's cue list to its last line.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six printed exercise cards where two of them stop mid cue, shipped to subscribers as the written reference for movements performed under load.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered seal survives at the size it is actually used. The trace is judged on screen at full canvas, where the ring's type, its inner rule and the anvil glyph all read cleanly. On the library sheet the seal sits small against the studio's deep ground, and at that reproduction size the thread nap the stitching raised becomes closed counters and a rule that merges into the type above it, so the mark reads as a dark blot rather than as a seal. Nothing in the trace's output, the export response or the first artboard reports it: the file is correct, its paths are all present, and at canvas size it is right. It is visible only by looking at the mark at its true reproduction size on the true ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the reproduction size is a property of the sheet's composition and the composition is downstream of the recovery; and getting it right first time would mean knowing how a specific stitched mark's stroke weight behaves at a size that has not been chosen yet. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the marks go on the cards and the sheet, and the acceptance line about readability at reproduction size is the client's standing requirement, not a hint that this trace closes. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a different upstream asset: re trace from a differently prepared raster where the nap has been resolved before tracing, or build the ring lockup from separate per element selections so the rule and the glyph carry their own weight, or reconsider the seal's size and its ground on the sheet, each of which is a different decision.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the patch raster to resolve the nap, re select the seal's elements separately rather than as one compound, re trace, re inject the viewBox and strip the ground path, then re place at reproduction size on the deep ground and look again before the sheet is called finished.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A library sheet and a card set carrying a certification seal that reads as a dark blot at every size a subscriber will ever see it, on the one element in the identity whose whole job is to signal credential.

deliverables.name: Anvil and Oak movement clips, landscape and vertical, with cleaned cue audio
deliverables.spec: Six landscape highlights, one per movement, each showing the movement performed correctly from setup through the working set and none of them reversed, plus six vertical companions for the short feed that reach their dimensions without a single added pixel, plus the coaching cue recording cleaned and judged as a continuous run. Every file named to the convention the app reads, with the source take recorded per movement and any movement that could not reach the short feed spec named rather than interpolated.

deliverables.name: Anvil and Oak poster frames
deliverables.spec: Six poster frames shot across two visits under two different ceiling banks brought to one studio white: one white point, one black point, one warmth, with the whitewashed wall reading as the same wall in all six, plus one licensed camera scale texture frame graded into the same world. Where a frame carries a cut subject the cut holds along the loaded bar as well as along the body. Per frame parameter log including one line on why each differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Recovered wordmark and certification seal
deliverables.spec: The studio wordmark and the compound ring seal recovered from a photograph of a stitched cloth patch as placeable scalable vector geometry with transparent grounds: real viewBoxes present, no opaque full canvas rectangles riding along, the seal carrying its inner rule and its central glyph with its counters open, delivered as single colour marks and colour accurate variants, and both holding at the size they actually reproduce on the card and small against the library sheet's deep ground.

deliverables.name: Exercise card run, first six movements

deliverables.name: Movement library reference sheet, as one editable document plus its source

Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the coaches extend the sheet each quarter and the source guarantees the design survives.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are moving, which are raster, which are a print run and which need an authored canvas the coaches extend themselves, given that the library grows every quarter.
Which take carries each movement, chosen from summaries of footage the agent did not film and judged on where the activity sits rather than on what is present.
Whether a given movement can reach the short feed's spec at all, or whether that source has to be swapped rather than reframed.

Whether the two photography visits can be brought to one studio white, how far to push the second visit's frames before the room stops looking like the room, and how to say so when one cannot be matched.
Which poster frames need the subject cut at all, and which route to cut them by where chrome meets whitewash.

Selection wording on the patch: naming the bag takes the canvas, naming each mark's own visual properties takes the thread, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the compound seal is taken as one selection or built from its parts, and whether the stitching's nap is texture worth keeping or noise to resolve before tracing.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a working studio register rather than a gym chain or a clinic, with the cue role decided for readability under load.
How the cue role's size and leading are set for the whole set once the longest record's real depth is known, versus re cutting copy with the coaches.
Whether a licensed texture frame joins the studio the six frames live in or reads as bought.
How the six movements are composed so the sheet reads as one library rather than six posters, and at what size each mark can sit and still read.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of people lifting weights. IDENTITY: these are these two coaches performing these six movements in their own barn gym, and the wordmark and seal have to be RECOVERED off the studio's own stitched patch rather than reinvented, because a regenerated seal is a credential nobody holds and a regenerated demonstration is not instruction, it is a picture of instruction. SPEC: six landscape clips and six verticals cut from supplied takes with a hard no added pixels rule and a naming convention the app parses, and a press file of exactly six pages in library order with each record's own frame bound to it and every cue list complete to its last line, none of which a generated image or clip satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the card template and the library sheet are defined by being extended, since six more movements arrive every quarter and the whole commission is a pipeline rather than an artifact. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality that only running produces: does this clip show the working set, does this cue list end where the record ends, does this seal still read small on the deep ground.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: only the four permitted Premiere operations are used, media_summarize to read takes, video_create_quick_cut which only ever shortens and is never asked to trim to a timestamp, video_resize which is never asked to enlarge, and media_enhance_speech; no compositing, no on screen text burn in, no motion graphics, no format conversion and no per artboard export appear anywhere in the trajectory, which is exactly why the real post's overlay ask was re carved into a printed and authored card set. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless. The mark checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumption: a compound mark selection returns the type ring and silently drops the inner rule and central element, remove_background hands back a solid opaque disc on an enclosed ring, and vectorize emits no viewBox and an opaque full canvas path at index zero, so the hygiene the acceptance bar scores is hygiene no tool performs. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with a per row image column bound through additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout are verified end to end, page count equal to row count is verified for PDF output, and the truncation checkpoint rests on a fixed frame inherited from a PDF derived template plus the documented fact that multi record raster order is misreported, which is why identity and completeness are checked on the page. No variable QR, no bleed claim, no named press preset and no high DPI expectation from the merge call itself. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, images must be embedded because references render as placeholders, and the rendition preview is documented as first artboard only. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, and the non standard numeric weight per family is why font_styles is mandatory. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returns genuine camera scale, and boards persist within a hard per call placement cap where a partial response means partial. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill, no object removal, no upscaling, no OCR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no vector render or vector merge, and no batch above twenty files.
